scope: Clarify conditional user impact for active refresh expiry, delayed delivery, and late timer cases.

answers.answer: Conditional yes. Continuous activity means a mouse event, then five seconds without another mouse event; it is not a five-second heartbeat. Each /extend response renews access only. It does not replace the refresh token. The candidate can show Timeout and logout when the original refresh token expires while access remains valid.
limits: The paired diagnostic controls provider responses and time.
The deployed environment and actual replacement frequency remain unverified.
network_actions: Home onMouseMove clears and restarts the five-second timer.
After five quiet seconds, the client sends POST /api/auth/v2/sso/extend.
The paired active-cutoff case sends zero POST /api/auth/v2/sso/refreshtoken requests.
At refresh expiry, the new version shows Timeout, sends logout requests, and shows Sign in.

answers.answer: The active-cutoff case is user-visible: Timeout appears, logout follows, and Sign in appears. A pending refresh request can be aborted during logout to reduce the stale-response race. Cancellation does not fix active cutoff because that case has no active refresh request at expiry. A session check is still required for responses that already completed.
limits: No production occurrence rate is established.
network_actions: Logout clears local state, but current logout does not abort that request.
A late response can store session-A refresh credentials.
After session B signs in, recovery can reuse the stale credential and clear session B.

answers.answer: Correct for delayed refresh delivery. Both versions receive a usable late refresh token, keep Extend disabled, send zero relogin requests, and logout. It remains a system defect.
limits: The comparison uses the shared scheduled-acquisition boundary.

answers.answer: The delayed-delivery case has no observed old/new behavior difference. The late-timer case changes internal behavior: old sends one refresh request and new sends zero. Access, refresh validity, and Timeout state remain equal in that controlled check. F-01 and F-03 still change user-visible behavior.
limits: The late-timer initial state is synthetic for the old Home journey.

production_timing_limit: The source configuration is not proof of the deployed environment. generateReToken adds 24,000 milliseconds to the configured refresh lifetime.
knowledge_update: Not applicable. This clarifies implementation impact without changing business policy.
